writeup.headline: Quest Diagnostics rates Hold: strong momentum and raised guidance offset by full valuation and leveraged balance sheet.
writeup.thesis: Quest scores 58, a Hold, seven points short of Buy. The strongest factor is trend (86): the price is 0.7% below its 52-week high, and the shares are 21.7 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. News is supportive (66) after Quest raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting revenues of $12.065-$12.105 billion, though a patient-data breach has prompted putative class actions. Growth is steady rather than fast, with TTM revenue growth of 9.1% and growth slowed by 0.2 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is solid, with a 14.6% operating margin, an 11.6% FCF margin and the diluted share count down 0.9% year on year. Holding the score back are the balance sheet (36), with net debt at 3.46x FCF and cash covering 0.14 of debt, and valuation (43): absolute multiples are moderate (19.7x P/FCF, 18.4x EV/EBIT, FCF yield 0.1 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield), and the stock is expensive against its own history.
key_risks: Valuation is expensive against its own history, with P/S more expensive than at 59 of the last 61 month-ends, leaving little cushion if growth slows.
The Quanum Lab Services Manager data breach and the resulting class actions could bring costs or regulatory action of unknown size.
Debt is meaningful: net debt is 3.46x FCF and cash covers only 0.14 of debt.
After a strong run (shares up 30.4% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago), the stock is vulnerable to a pullback if momentum fades.
Revenue growth slowed by 0.2 pp, and a further slowdown in requisition volumes would weaken the growth case.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (7 points needed): faster revenue growth, or a valuation pullback that lifts the valuation score from 43, while trend holds up.
Up: paying down debt to improve the balance sheet score from 36.
Down to Sell (14 points away): a sharp reversal in price trend combined with worse news, such as large breach-related liabilities or a guidance cut.
Down: margin pressure that pulls the quality score below its current 62.
